turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you, Doctor. I came in because... well, it's my husband’s sister. She has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. And she thinks I don't notice! Just like last week, she came over bringing these cheap store-bought muffins. Who brings store-bought muffins when they know I bake? I've been baking since I was in middle school, right before I left school to help my mom out at home. I make a blueberry buckle that won a blue ribbon once at the county fair, you know. I use real butter, none of that margarine nonsense. But anyway, no matter how folks try to smooth it over and tell me she's just trying to be helpful, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. She wants the money and she wants me gone.

If I'd had a boy, I would have named him Michael. But we never had children. Just a house full of cats. We have three right now: Fluffy, Whiskers, and Barnaby. Barnaby is a terror, always knocking things off the counter. Just yesterday he broke my favorite coffee mug, the one I got in Florida... but no, no voices in my head, if that's what you mean. I ended up just going to the grocery store instead. The grocery store is always so crowded on Tuesdays, though, because of the senior discount. I'm not quite old enough for it yet, but my neighbor Mildred is. She always goes on Tuesdays and brings back those little bakery cookies... but no, I'm not wrong about my sister-in-law. The man who owned the factory, Mr. Henderson, he was such a fair boss. Every Christmas he'd give us all a turkey and a tin of those Danish butter cookies. The ones in the blue tin? turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I've always been a pretty trusting person, really. I mean, my friends and I, we've known each other for years. We'd spend all day in the hot kitchen, putting up peaches and green beans... but no, I've never had any trouble with my friends or my own side of the family. It's just her.

I used to love watching the robins splash around in it in the mornings while I drank my coffee. I only drink one cup a day now, though, doctor said it was better for my stomach. But anyway... no, I don't distrust people in general. I just know what I see with her.

Deviled eggs always give me heartburn now, which is a shame because I make a wonderful deviled egg. The secret is just a tiny pinch of dry mustard and a splash of pickle juice. Sweet pickle juice, not dill. Dill is too sharp. I tried making dill pickles once, grew the cucumbers myself on a trellis by the back fence.
